packet.headline_seed: Tesla driver in fatal Texas crash pressed accelerator 100%, NTSB confirms
packet.description_seed: The safety board confirmed Tesla's account of the crash, which the company shared days after it happened last month.

what: Tesla driver in fatal Texas crash pressed accelerator 100%, NTSB confirms

clean_source_blocks.text: The safety board confirmed Tesla's account of the crash, which the company shared days after it happened last month.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said Wednesday that the driver of a Tesla who crashed into a house in June had pressed the accelerator pedal to 100%, overriding the company’s Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software. Data recovered from the Tesla showed that the vehicle was traveling more than 70 miles per hour when it struck a house in Katy, Texas, killing 76-year-old resident Martha Avila, according to the NTSB. The family of the victim has since sued the alleged driver, 44-year-old Michael Butler, and Tesla, claiming negligence. Butler has also been charged with manslaughter. ---

Tesla now confirms that its self-driving system was engaged when a Model 3 left a residential road in Katy, Texas, and killed a 76-year-old woman inside her home — but the company says the driver overrode it by pressing the accelerator to 100%. Everything points to a pedal misapplication while the car was under “Full Self-Driving.” Does that mean Tesla is not at fault? Tesla’s Head of AI, Ashok Elluswamy, said the company’s vehicle data shows driver Michael Butler “manually overrode self-driving by pressing the accelerator all the way to 100% of the accel pedal in this residential area.” According to Tesla, the Model 3 reached 73 mph with the accelerator floored, and the pedal was still pressed even after the car had plowed through the brick home.

Tesla didn’t respond to WIRED’s request for comment. But on X, Tesla vice president of AI software Ashok Elluswamy wrote that Tesla data showed that Butler “manually overrode self-driving by pressing the accelerator all the way to 100 percent” and “had the accelerator pressed even after the crash.” Tesla CEO Elon Musk posted that speculation that the company’s technology played a role in the crash “makes no sense.” Plenty of the crash’s specifics have yet to come out, and it’s very possible that Tesla’s tech didn’t have anything to do with Avila’s death. But even if the driver is mostly responsible for what happened, the electric-auto maker could still be found at least partially culpable—and liable for big monetary damages.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said Wednesday that the driver of a Tesla who crashed into a house in June had pressed the accelerator pedal to 100%, overriding the company’s Full Self-Driving (Supervised) software.

Data recovered from the Tesla showed that the vehicle was traveling more than 70 miles per hour when it struck a house in Katy, Texas, killing 76-year-old resident Martha Avila, according to the NTSB. The family of the victim has since sued the alleged driver, 44-year-old Michael Butler, and Tesla, claiming negligence. Butler has also been charged with manslaughter.

---

[Lähde: Wired | URL: https://www.wired.com/story/a-fatal-tesla-crash-in-texas-sets-up-a-legal-showdown/]
On a Texas evening last week, a 76-year-old grandmother named Martha Avila was standing in the front room of her suburban home when a Tesla Model 3 hurtled into her brick home at a reported speed of over 70 miles per hour, killing her.

The car’s driver, 44-year-old Michael Butler, later told police that he had Tesla’s driver assistance features—which the automaker argues make driving safer and less stressful—engaged during the crash. Butler exhibited “no signs of intoxication,” the Harris County Sheriff’s Office, which responded to the crash, noted in a report.

Now Avila’s family is suing not only Butler but also Tesla, alleging that the electric-auto maker's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) driver assistance feature, also called FSD, played a role in her death. The feature is designed to handle certain aspects of driving—including navigating city and residential roads, stopping for red lights and stop signs, and changing lanes—but it requires drivers to pay attention and stay ready to intervene if the system makes a mistake. The suit alleges Tesla’s tech “was defective in design and unreasonably dangerous,” lawyers representing Avila’s daughter and son-in-law wrote in a lawsuit filed in Harris County District Court on Tuesday. (The son-in-law, Justin Barbour, was also in the home and injured in the crash.)

Tesla didn’t respond to WIRED’s request for comment. But on X, Tesla vice president of AI software Ashok Elluswamy wrote that Tesla data showed that Butler “manually overrode self-driving by pressing the accelerator all the way to 100 percent” and “had the accelerator pressed even after the crash.” Tesla CEO Elon Musk posted that speculation that the company’s technology played a role in the crash “makes no sense.”

Plenty of the crash’s specifics have yet to come out, and it’s very possible that Tesla’s tech didn’t have anything to do with Avila’s death. But even if the driver is mostly responsible for what happened, the electric-auto maker could still be found at least partially culpable—and liable for big monetary damages.

payload.title: NTSB: Tesla-auton kuljettaja painoi kaasupolkimen pohjaan kuolemaan johtaneessa törmäyksessä
payload.summary: NTSB:n mukaan kuljettajan täysi kaasupolkimen painallus ohitti Teslan valvotun ajoavustinohjelmiston. Auto törmäsi Texasissa asuintaloon, ja 76-vuotias Martha Avila kuoli.
payload.content:
Yhdysvaltain liikenneturvallisuuslautakunta NTSB:n mukaan Tesla-auton kuljettaja painoi kaasupolkimen täysin pohjaan, mikä ohitti auton valvotun Full Self-Driving -järjestelmän ennen kesäkuista törmäystä Katyn kaupungissa Texasissa. Model 3 osui suurella nopeudella asuintaloon, ja törmäyksessä kuoli kodissaan ollut 76-vuotias Martha Avila.

Ajoneuvodata vahvisti täyden painalluksen

NTSB kertoi keskiviikkona 15. heinäkuuta, että ajoneuvosta talteen saadut tiedot osoittivat kaasupolkimen olleen painettuna 100-prosenttisesti. Täysi painallus ohitti auton Full Self-Driving (Supervised) -ohjelmiston. Lautakunnan mukaan auto kulki yli 70 mailia eli yli 110 kilometriä tunnissa osuessaan taloon.

Tesla oli esittänyt saman kuvauksen jo päiviä onnettomuuden jälkeen. Yhtiön tekoälyohjelmistoista vastaavan johtajan Ashok Elluswamyn mukaan Model 3 saavutti 73 mailin eli noin 117 kilometrin tuntinopeuden kaasupolkimen ollessa pohjassa. Tesla kertoi polkimen pysyneen painettuna vielä senkin jälkeen, kun auto oli ajanut tiilisen talon läpi.

NTSB:n julkistama tieto koskee täyttä painallusta, ohjelmiston ohittumista ja törmäysnopeutta. Väite siitä, että poljin pysyi painettuna vielä taloon osumisen jälkeen, perustuu Teslan omaan kuvaukseen ajoneuvodatasta.

Teslan vastuu jää avoimeksi

Avilan perhe on nostanut kanteen auton väitettyä kuljettajaa, 44-vuotiasta Michael Butleria, sekä Teslaa vastaan. Kanteessa molempia syytetään huolimattomuudesta. Butleria vastaan on lisäksi nostettu syyte kuolemantuottamuksesta. Perheen väitteitä Teslan vastuusta ei ole vielä ratkaistu.

Tesla ei vastannut Wired-lehden kommenttipyyntöön, mutta Elluswamy julkaisi yhtiön dataa koskevan selostuksen X-palvelussa. Teslan toimitusjohtaja Elon Musk puolestaan kirjoitti, ettei väite yhtiön teknologian osuudesta onnettomuuteen hänen mielestään käy järkeen.

NTSB:n ilmoitus vahvistaa Teslan aiemmin julkaiseman kuvauksen kaasupolkimen painamisesta ja auton nopeudesta. Se ei kuitenkaan ratkaise, miten oikeudellinen vastuu jakautuu kuljettajan ja autonvalmistajan välillä. Tapauksen kaikkia yksityiskohtia ei ole julkistettu, ja uhrin perheen kanteessa arvioitavaksi jää myös se, voiko Tesla olla osittain vastuussa, vaikka kuljettajan toiminta oli välitön syy järjestelmän ohittamiseen.
summary_bullets: NTSB:n mukaan täysi kaasupolkimen painallus ohitti Teslan valvotun ajoavustinohjelmiston.
Model 3 törmäsi yli 110 kilometrin tuntinopeudella taloon, jossa 76-vuotias Martha Avila kuoli.
Avilan perhe on haastanut sekä kuljettajan että Teslan oikeuteen huolimattomuudesta.
